question: What is the 16MB document size limit in MongoDB, and what architectural pattern addresses it? What is the 16MB document size limit in MongoDB, and what architectural pattern addresses it?

options.text: MongoDB caps single BSON documents at 16MB. The Time-Series Bucket Pattern or 1:N referencing solves unbounded array growth.
MongoDB caps single BSON documents at 16MB, and the fix is to enable {allowDiskUse: true} so oversized documents spill to temporary files on disk instead of being rejected.
MongoDB caps single BSON documents at 100MB, and the Time-Series Bucket Pattern is only needed once a collection's total size exceeds several terabytes.
The 16MB limit applies only to documents returned by a query, not to documents stored on disk, so an oversized array only becomes a problem when it is read back.

explanation: Specification answer: MongoDB caps single BSON documents at 16MB. The Time-Series Bucket Pattern or 1:N referencing solves unbounded array growth.

question: Explain the structural components of a 12-byte BSON ObjectId.? Explain the structural components of a 12-byte BSON ObjectId.

options.text: 4 bytes unix epoch timestamp, 5 bytes random value unique to machine/process, and 3 bytes incrementing counter.
8 bytes unix epoch timestamp with millisecond precision, and 4 bytes of a purely random value with no counter component at all.
4 bytes incrementing counter, 4 bytes machine identifier, and 4 bytes process id, with no timestamp component.
12 bytes of a cryptographically secure random value, generated fresh for every document with no embedded timestamp or counter.

explanation: Specification answer: 4 bytes unix epoch timestamp, 5 bytes random value unique to machine/process, and 3 bytes incrementing counter.

question: When should you Embed vs Reference related data in MongoDB? When should you Embed vs Reference related data in MongoDB?

options.text: Embed for 1:1 or bounded 1:N relationships accessed together atomically; Reference for unbounded 1:N or M:N relationships updated independently.
Always embed related data regardless of relationship size, since MongoDB has no meaningful limit on array length in practice.
Reference should be used for 1:1 relationships accessed together atomically, while embedding is reserved for large, unbounded M:N relationships to save storage.
The choice between embedding and referencing only affects read performance, never write performance, so it can be changed freely at any time without a migration.

explanation: Specification answer: Embed for 1:1 or bounded 1:N relationships accessed together atomically; Reference for unbounded 1:N or M:N relationships updated independently.

question: What is a TTL (Time-To-Live) index in MongoDB? What is a TTL (Time-To-Live) index in MongoDB?

options.text: A single-field index on a date field that automatically deletes documents after a specified number of seconds via a background reaper thread.
A compound index on a date field and a boolean 'expired' flag that an application cron job must check and delete manually; MongoDB does not delete documents automatically.
An index that limits how long a query is allowed to run before it is automatically cancelled by the server, unrelated to document lifetime.
A single-field index on a date field that prevents any document older than the specified number of seconds from being inserted in the first place.

explanation: Specification answer: A single-field index on a date field that automatically deletes documents after a specified number of seconds via a background reaper thread.

question:
During triage in MongoDB Document Modeling BSON, an engineer observes:
"System fault during operation: BSONObjectTooLarge Error on Unbounded Sensor Array".
What is the verified root cause?

options.text: IoT readings appended continuously into a single document array without capping, eventually breaching the 16MB document size limit.

The sensor readings are stored correctly in separate documents, but a poorly designed aggregation pipeline uses $group to reassemble them into one oversized in-memory result before returning it to the client.
Each sensor reading is stored as its own tiny document, and the 16MB limit was hit by the total size of the collection's index on sensor_id, not by any single document.
A change stream watching the sensor collection buffers every update event in an unbounded in-memory queue on the application side, and that queue, not any MongoDB document, is what exceeded 16MB.

explanation:
Root Cause: IoT readings appended continuously into a single document array without capping, eventually breaching the 16MB document size limit.

Fix Resolution:
Implement the Time-Series Bucket Pattern: store at most 500 readings per document bucket and insert a new document when bucket reaches capacity.
